subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: What Is a Heat Engine?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is a Heat Engine?.

hook.text: Every car, power plant, and jet converts heat into motion. That conversion is what a heat engine does.

buildup.text: A heat engine takes in thermal energy, converts part of it to work, and dumps the rest as waste heat.

discovery.text: You need a hot source and a cold sink. The temperature difference is what drives the work output.

twist.text: No heat engine can convert all heat to work. Some energy must always be rejected to the cold side.

climax.text: This isn't a design flaw — it's a law of physics. The second law of thermodynamics guarantees waste.

punchline.text: Heat engines run on difference. No gap, no work.

quiz.question: Why can't a heat engine convert all heat into useful work?
options: Engineers haven't found efficient enough materials yet
The second law of thermodynamics requires waste heat rejection
Friction in moving parts always consumes all the excess energy
